headline: A 2018 law lets the Department of Agriculture give Old Town, Maine, back certain federal land rights at no cost for economic development.
what_it_does: The law directs the Department of Agriculture to release the federal government's remaining rights in certain lands it had given to Old Town, Maine, in 1941 under the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act. The release happens only if the city asks in writing and plans to transfer the land for economic development. The federal government would transfer these rights without charging the city any money.

who_it_affects.how: The city can request in writing that the federal government give up its remaining interest in the 1941 lands so it can transfer them for economic development without a federal payment.
The department must release its interest in these lands when the city makes a qualifying written request.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses or developers who may later acquire the land
who_it_affects.how: Land that the city proposes to transfer for economic development would no longer carry the federal government's original 1941 restrictions and interest.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on March 26, 2018, but the land release happens only after the city makes a written request for lands it proposes to transfer for economic development.
